words.tr:
n. 工序；过程；
v. 处理；加工；
words.ex: The factory improved the production process.
words.ex_cn: 工厂改进了生产工序。
words.en: A process is a series of actions which are carried out in order to achieve a particular result.

words.tr:
n. 制造；
v. （用机器大量）制造；虚构；捏造；
words.ex: The manufacture of cars needs many workers.
words.ex_cn: 汽车的制造需要很多工人。
words.en: To manufacture something means to make it in a factory, usually in large quantities.

words.tr:
v. 生产；制造；导致；引起；生育；出示；
n. 农产品；
words.ex: The farm produces fresh vegetables every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个农场每天生产新鲜蔬菜。
words.en: To produce something means to make, create, or manufacture it, often in large quantities. It can also refer to the act of causing something to happen or exist.

words.tr:
v. 治疗；对待；
n. 款待；
words.ex: The doctor will treat his fever with medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生会用药物治疗他的发烧。
words.en: If you treat someone or something in a particular way, you behave towards them or deal with them in that way.

words.ex: He refines his writing every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天完善自己的写作。
words.en: To refine something means to make it purer or to improve it, especially by removing unwanted substances or by making small changes.

words.tr:
v. 切；割；削减；
n. 切；割；削减；
words.ex: He cut the apple with a knife.
words.ex_cn: 他用刀切了苹果。
words.en: To make an opening, incision, or wound in (something) with a sharp-edged tool or object.

words.tr: n. 切片；薄片；部分；片段；
words.ex: She ate a slice of bread for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 她早餐吃了一片面包。
words.en: A slice of something is a thin piece or portion of it.

words.ex: The boys are playing dice after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后玩掷骰游戏。
words.en: Small cubes marked on each side with spots numbering from one to six, used in games of chance; to cut food into small cubes.

words.ex: He chopped the carrots into small pieces.
words.ex_cn: 他把胡萝卜剁成了小块。
words.en: To chop something means to cut it into pieces with a sharp tool such as a knife or axe. It can also refer to the act of reducing something in amount or size.

words.ex: He always keeps his garden trim and neat.
words.ex_cn: 他总是把花园打理得整洁有序。
words.en: To trim something means to make it tidier or more level by cutting a small amount off it.

words.tr:
n. 形状；身材；定形；
v. 塑造；
words.ex: The shape of the table is round.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子的形状是圆形的。
words.en: The shape of an object is its external form or outline, which can be seen and felt.

words.tr:
n. 形式；表格；形状；
v. 组成；建立；
words.ex: The form of the poem is very simple.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的形式非常简单。
words.en: A form is a particular way in which a thing exists or appears, or a document with spaces in which to write information.

words.ex: The baker used a metal mold to shape the cake.
words.ex_cn: 面包师用一个金属模具来塑造蛋糕。
words.en: A mold is a hollow container used to give shape to molten or hot liquid material when it cools and hardens. It can also refer to a fungus that grows on food or damp surfaces.

words.tr:
n. 全体演员；
v. 投掷；扔；投射；
words.ex: The cast of the play performed very well.
words.ex_cn: 这部剧的全体演员表演得非常好。
words.en: To cast something means to throw it forcefully in a particular direction.

words.tr:
n. 轮廓；外形；等高线
v. 画轮廓（画等高线）
adj. 显示轮廓的
words.ex: The map shows the contour of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图显示了山的轮廓。
words.en: The outline of a figure, body, or mass, especially the curved shape of a surface.

words.ex: He will assemble the toy for his son.
words.ex_cn: 他将为儿子组装玩具。
words.en: If people assemble or if someone assembles them, they come together in a group, usually for a particular purpose such as a meeting.

words.tr:
v. 建造；构造；
n. 概念；
words.ex: They construct houses with bricks.
words.ex_cn: 他们用砖块建造房屋。
words.en: To construct something means to build or create it, usually something large such as a building, road, or machine.

words.tr:
v. 建筑；建造；逐步加强；
n. 体格；体形；
words.ex: They build a house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他们在湖边建了一所房子。
words.en: To construct something by putting parts or material together.

words.tr: phrase. 组成整体；装配；组合
words.ex: He put together a sandwich for lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他做了个三明治当午餐。
words.en: To assemble or compile various parts or elements into a whole.

words.tr:
v. 符合；合身；
adj. 健康的；适合的；
words.ex: This shirt fits me well.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫很合我的身。
words.en: If something fits, it is the right size and shape to go onto a person's body or onto a particular object.

words.ex: We work together every day.
words.ex_cn: 我们每天一起工作。
words.en: If people do something together, they do it with each other.

words.tr:
v. 提取；
n. 摘录；提取物；
words.ex: They extract oil from plants.
words.ex_cn: 他们从植物中提取油。
words.en: To remove or take out something, especially by effort or force.

words.ex: The hospital will isolate the patient to stop the spread.
words.ex_cn: 医院将隔离这名病人以防止传播。
words.en: To isolate someone or something means to separate them from other people or things, often in order to protect them or to prevent the spread of something harmful.

words.ex: The machine purifies water by removing dirt.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器通过去除杂质来净化水。
words.en: To purify something means to make it clean and pure by removing dirty or harmful substances from it.

words.tr: v. 蒸馏；用蒸馏法提取；蒸馏出；提炼
words.ex: They distill water to remove impurities.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过蒸馏去除水中的杂质。
words.en: To distill a liquid means to purify it by heating it until it becomes a gas and then cooling it so that it becomes a liquid again. This process can also be used to extract the essential elements or meanings from something.

words.ex: The workers fix the production line every morning.
words.ex_cn: 工人们每天早上修理生产线。
words.en: A sequence of machines and workers in a factory where products are assembled step by step.

words.ex: The workers fixed the manufacturing line after it broke.
words.ex_cn: 工人在生产线坏了之后进行了维修。
words.en: A system of machines and processes for making goods in a factory, often involving automated stages.

words.ex: He works on the assembly line in a car factory.
words.ex_cn: 他在汽车工厂的生产线上工作。
words.en: A production line where parts are added to a product in a fixed sequence as it moves along.

words.ex: The factory uses a conveyor belt system to move boxes.
words.ex_cn: 工厂使用传送带系统移动箱子。

words.ex: The reactor produces electricity for the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个反应堆为城市发电。
words.en: A reactor is a device or structure in which nuclear fission or fusion reactions are initiated, controlled, and sustained.

words.ex: The fishing vessel sailed out at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 那艘渔船在黎明时出海。
words.en: A vessel is a large boat or a container for holding liquids.

words.tr: n. 房间；室；腔；大会议室；
words.ex: He sat in the chamber and waited quietly.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在房间里安静地等待。
words.en: A chamber is a large room, especially one that is used for formal or public events.

words.ex: The crucible melted the metal under high heat.
words.ex_cn: 坩埚在高温下熔化了金属。
words.en: A crucible is a pot in which metals or other substances are heated to a very high temperature or melted. It can also refer to a severe test or trial.

words.ex: She put the kettle on to make tea.
words.ex_cn: 她把水壶放在炉子上烧水泡茶。
words.en: A kettle is a container or device in which water is boiled, having a lid, spout, and handle, used for making tea or coffee.

words.tr: n. 切割者；切割机；裁切器；小汽艇
words.ex: The cutter sliced the bread with a sharp knife.
words.ex_cn: 切割者用锋利的刀切开了面包。
words.en: A cutter is someone or something that cuts, especially a tool or machine used for cutting materials.

words.ex: I saw a bird fly over the house.
words.ex_cn: 我看到一只鸟飞过房子。
words.en: A saw is a tool consisting of a tough blade, wire, or chain with a hard toothed edge. It is used to cut through material, very often wood, though sometimes metal or stone. The cut is made by placing the toothed edge against the material and moving it forcefully forth and less forcefully back or continuously forward.

words.ex: He used a slicer to cut the cheese into thin pieces.
words.ex_cn: 他用切片机把奶酪切成薄片。
words.en: A slicer is a tool or machine used for cutting something into thin, flat pieces.

words.ex: He hit the wood with a chopper.
words.ex_cn: 他用斧头砍木头。
words.en: A chopper is a type of helicopter or a large knife used for cutting meat or wood.

words.tr:
n. 断头台；切纸机
v. 处斩刑
words.ex: The king was killed by the guillotine.
words.ex_cn: 国王被断头台处决了。
words.en: A guillotine is a device used for carrying out executions by decapitation. It consists of a tall, upright frame in which a weighted and angled blade is raised to the top and suspended. The condemned person is secured with stocks at the bottom of the frame, positioning the neck directly below the blade. The blade is then released, swiftly and forcefully decapitating the victim with a single, clean pass.

words.ex: The old tree died last winter.
words.ex_cn: 那棵老树去年冬天死了。
words.en: To die means to stop living and become dead.

words.tr:
n. 新闻界；出版社；
v. 按；压；
words.ex: The press reported the news quickly.
words.ex_cn: 新闻界迅速报道了这则新闻。
words.en: To press something is to push it firmly, often with your fingers or hand, in order to operate a device or machine, or to make something flat or smooth. It can also mean to urge someone to do something or to make a strong demand for something.

words.ex: He put a stamp on the envelope.
words.ex_cn: 他在信封上贴了一张邮票。
words.en: A stamp is a small piece of paper which you stick on an envelope or package before you post it to pay for the cost of the postage. It can also mean to bring down your foot heavily on the ground or to impress a pattern or mark on a surface.

words.ex: The matrix gave birth to all living things.
words.ex_cn: 母体孕育了所有生命。
words.en: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers, symbols, or expressions, arranged in rows and columns.

words.ex: He sings and plays guitar simultaneously.
words.ex_cn: 他一边唱歌一边弹吉他。
words.en: If two or more things happen simultaneously, they happen at exactly the same time.

words.ex: He works and studies concurrently.
words.ex_cn: 他同时工作和学习。
words.en: At the same time; simultaneously.

words.ex: He walked alongside the river.
words.ex_cn: 他沿着河边走。
words.en: If one thing is alongside another thing, the first thing is next to the second.

words.ex: The two boys sat side by side on the bench.
words.ex_cn: 两个男孩并排坐在长凳上。
words.en: If two or more things are side by side, they are next to each other.

words.ex: The seedling stage is when the plant starts to grow from the seed.
words.ex_cn: 幼苗期是植物从种子开始生长的时候。
words.en: The early growth phase of a plant after germination, when the first true leaves develop.

words.ex: The germination period of the seed is two weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这种种子的发芽期是两周。
words.en: The time during which a seed sprouts and begins to grow, typically requiring water, warmth, and oxygen.

words.tr: n. 青少年时期；幼年阶段
words.ex: The juvenile phase of the dog lasts about one year.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗的幼年期持续大约一年。
words.en: The intermediate growth stage of a plant between seedling and maturity, characterized by rapid development.

words.ex: The plant is in its flowering stage.
words.ex_cn: 这株植物正处于开花阶段。
words.en: The phase in a plant's life cycle when buds form and flowers begin to open.

words.ex: The blossoming period of the cherry trees is in spring.
words.ex_cn: 樱花的盛开期在春天。
words.en: The period during which flowers are fully open and at their most attractive, often for pollination.

words.tr: n. 花卉展览；花艺展示
words.ex: The hotel has a beautiful floral display in the lobby.
words.ex_cn: 酒店大堂有一个美丽的花卉陈列。
words.en: The collective display of flowers on a plant, often used to attract pollinators or for ornamental value.

words.tr: n. 结果期；果实成熟阶段
words.ex: The plant is in the fruiting stage.
words.ex_cn: 这株植物正处于结果阶段。
words.en: The phase in a plant's life cycle when flowers develop into mature fruits.

words.ex: The ripening period of this apple is 90 days.
words.ex_cn: 这种苹果的成熟期是90天。
words.en: The time during which fruits or crops mature and become ready for picking.

words.tr: n. 收获季节；收获时期
words.ex: Farmers work hard during harvesttime.
words.ex_cn: 农民在收获季节辛勤工作。
words.en: The season or period when crops are gathered from the fields.

words.tr: n. [动]蜕皮；换羽; v. 脱毛；换羽（molt 的 ing 形式）
words.ex: The snake is molting, which is why its skin looks loose.
words.ex_cn: 这条蛇正在蜕皮，所以它的皮肤看起来很松弛。
words.en: Molting is the process by which an animal sheds its old feathers, hair, or skin to make way for new growth.

words.ex: The process of ecdysis allows the snake to grow larger.
words.ex_cn: 蜕皮过程使蛇能够长得更大。
words.en: Ecdysis is the process of shedding the old skin (in reptiles) or outer cuticle (in insects and other arthropods) in order to grow.

words.tr: v. 蜕皮；流出； n. 脱落，蜕落 v. 流出( shed的现在分词 )；
words.ex: The snake is shedding its skin.
words.ex_cn: 蛇正在蜕皮。
words.en: The process of losing or getting rid of something, such as hair, leaves, or skin, because it is no longer needed or wanted.

words.tr: v. 脱落；剥落；（皮肤）脱皮；（旧时）使...脱水；（动物）脱壳
words.ex: The snake is sloughing its old skin.
words.ex_cn: 蛇正在蜕皮。
words.en: The process of shedding or peeling off an outer layer, such as skin or bark.

words.ex: Birds begin migration in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类在秋天开始迁徙。
words.en: The movement of people, animals, or birds from one place to another, especially regularly according to the seasons.

words.ex: His emigration to Canada changed his life.
words.ex_cn: 他移民到加拿大改变了人生。
words.en: Emigration is the act of leaving one's own country to settle permanently in another; moving abroad.

words.ex: The relocation of the factory caused many job changes.
words.ex_cn: 工厂的迁移导致了许多工作变动。
words.en: The act of moving to a new place and establishing one's home or business there.

words.tr: v. 徘徊；漫游；“wander”的现在分词；
words.ex: He was wandering in the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后在公园里徘徊。
words.en: If you describe a person or their thoughts as wandering, you mean that the person is not concentrating on anything in particular and their thoughts are not clear.

words.tr: v. 旅游；旅行；“travel”的现在分词； n. 旅行；旅游；游历； adj. 旅行的；巡回的；旅行用的；
words.ex: I love traveling to new countries.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢去新的国家旅游。
words.en: Moving or going from one place to another, especially over a long distance.

words.ex: Bears go into hibernation in winter.
words.ex_cn: 熊在冬天冬眠。
words.en: Hibernation is a state of inactivity and metabolic depression in endotherms during winter.

words.ex: The cold weather put the animal into torpor.
words.ex_cn: 寒冷的天气让动物陷入麻木状态。
words.en: a state of physical or mental inactivity; lethargy.

words.tr: n. 冬眠（尤指爬行动物的冬眠）
words.ex: Snakes undergo brumation during cold winter months.
words.ex_cn: 蛇在寒冷的冬季会进入冬眠。
words.en: A state of dormancy in cold-blooded animals, similar to hibernation, during winter.

words.tr: n. 冬眠（指某些动物在冬季的休眠状态）
words.ex: Bears go into wintersleep when it gets cold.
words.ex_cn: 当天气变冷时，熊会进入冬眠。
words.en: A prolonged period of inactivity or dormancy in animals during the winter months.

words.ex: The plant is in dormancy during winter.
words.ex_cn: 这株植物在冬天处于休眠状态。
words.en: A state of rest or inactivity, often associated with a period of suspended development or growth.

words.ex: The texture of the bread is soft and fluffy.
words.ex_cn: 这种面包的质地柔软蓬松。
words.en: The feel, appearance, or consistency of a surface or a substance.

words.ex: Farmers grow grain like wheat and rice.
words.ex_cn: 农民种植小麦和大米等谷物。
words.en: A grain is a small, hard seed of a food plant such as wheat, rice, or corn, or the plant itself.

words.ex: He really loves his job.
words.ex_cn: 他真正地热爱他的工作。
words.en: You use really to emphasize that something is true or that it is the case.

words.tr: n. 始终一贯；前后一致；
words.ex: His consistency in studying every day helped him pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他每天学习的一贯坚持帮助他通过了考试。
words.en: Consistency is the quality or condition of being consistent, especially in achieving a level of performance or behavior that does not vary greatly in quality over time.

words.ex: The smoothness of the ice made it easy to skate.
words.ex_cn: 冰面的平滑使滑冰变得容易。
words.en: The quality or state of being smooth, without roughness or bumps, or moving without difficulty or interruption.

words.ex: The book has a gloss at the bottom of each page.
words.ex_cn: 这本书每页底部都有注释。
words.en: A gloss is a bright shine on the surface of something. It can also refer to a superficial appearance or interpretation that conceals the true nature of something.

words.ex: The sun shines brightly in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在早晨明亮地发光。
words.en: To emit or reflect light brightly; to be very good at something.

words.tr: n. 光泽；光亮；光辉 n. 光泽；光亮；光辉
words.ex: The silver ring lost its luster after years of use.
words.ex_cn: 这枚银戒指在多年使用后失去了光泽。
words.en: The quality of having a soft glow or sheen; brightness and shine.

words.tr:
n. 光泽；上光剂；
v. 擦亮；润色；
words.ex: The polish of the wooden table made it shine.
words.ex_cn: 木桌的光泽让它闪闪发亮。
words.en: If you polish something, you make it smooth and shiny by rubbing it with a cloth or a special substance. Polish is also a substance that you use to make things smooth and shiny.

words.tr: n. 行为特征；性格特点
words.ex: Dogs show behavioral traits like loyalty and playfulness.
words.ex_cn: 狗表现出忠诚和爱玩等行为特征。
words.en: Observable and measurable patterns of behavior in an organism.

words.ex: His behavior at the party was very polite.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上的举止非常礼貌。
words.en: The way in which one acts or conducts oneself, especially towards others.

words.ex: He has good habits every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都有好习惯。
words.en: A habit is something that you do often or regularly.

words.ex: The characteristics of this animal include long legs and big ears.
words.ex_cn: 这种动物的特征包括长腿和大耳朵。
words.en: A characteristic is a quality or feature that is typical of someone or something.

words.ex: His nature is kind and patient.
words.ex_cn: 他的本性是善良且有耐心的。
words.en: Nature refers to the physical world and everything in it that is not made by people, including plants, animals, mountains, oceans, stars, etc. It can also refer to the basic or inherent features, character, or qualities of something.

words.ex: The product is in the launch lifecyclestage.
words.ex_cn: 这个产品正处于发布阶段。
words.en: A distinct period in the existence of an organism, from birth to death.

words.ex: The child is in a critical developmental phase.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子正处于一个关键的发展阶段。
words.en: A specific stage in the process of growth and maturation of an organism.

words.tr: adj. 个体发生的；个体发育的
words.ex: The study focuses on the ontogenetic development of the species.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究集中在该物种的个体发育过程上。
words.en: Relating to the origin and development of an individual organism.

words.tr:
n. 阶段；时期；舞台；
v. 举行；上演；
words.ex: This is a critical stage in his recovery.
words.ex_cn: 这是他康复过程中的一个关键阶段。
words.en: A stage is a raised area in a theatre or hall where performers, speakers, or entertainers stand. It can also refer to a particular point or period in the development or progress of something.

words.ex: The temperature shows seasonal variations.
words.ex_cn: 温度显示出季节性的变化。
words.en: Changes in conditions or patterns that occur at particular times of the year.

words.tr: n. 季节性的波动；季节性变化
words.ex: The store sales show seasonal fluctuations.
words.ex_cn: 商店的销售额显示出季节性波动。
words.en: Regular, predictable changes in data or activity that happen over the course of a year.

words.ex: The store sells seasonal fruits like strawberries in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店在春天出售草莓等季节性水果。
words.en: Seasonal means relating to or happening during a particular season.

words.ex: The children noticed patterns in the tiles on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们注意到了地板瓷砖上的模式。
words.en: Designs or motifs that are repeated in a predictable sequence.

words.tr: n. 气候变化；气候差异
words.ex: The plants survive due to climatic variations.
words.ex_cn: 这些植物由于气候的变化而存活。
words.en: Long-term changes in weather patterns, especially over decades or centuries.

words.tr: adv. 紧接着的；紧接着地
words.ex: He left the room immediately following the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他会议一结束就离开了房间。
words.en: Occurring directly after something in time or sequence.

words.tr: adj. 接下来的；随后的；按照之前的步骤
words.ex: Follow the following step to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 按照接下来的步骤来解决问题。
words.en: Taking place directly after the preceding action or phase in a process.

words.tr: phrase. 最初地；首先地 adv. 主要地；首要地；根本上
words.ex: He initially liked math, but primarily enjoys science now.
words.ex_cn: 他最初喜欢数学，但现在主要喜欢科学。
words.en: At the beginning; primarily or mainly in the early stages of a process or development.

words.ex: She likes reading books; additionally, she writes stories too.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢读书；此外，她还写故事。
words.en: Used to add another point or piece of information to what has already been said.

words.ex: He worked hard, and ultimately succeeded.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作，最终成功了。
words.en: You use ultimately to indicate that something is the final result of a series of events or the most important part of a situation.

words.ex: He started running after the initial stage.
words.ex_cn: 他在初始阶段之后开始跑步。
words.en: Happening after the first phase or period of a process or event.

words.tr: n. 进入下一阶段；进展到下一阶段
words.ex: He is moving to the next stage of the project.
words.ex_cn: 他正在进入项目的下一阶段。
words.en: Progressing to the subsequent phase or step in a sequence.

words.ex: He left the room immediately after the bell rang.
words.ex_cn: 铃声一响，他就离开了房间。
words.en: Occurring without any interval of time after a preceding event or action.

words.ex: He left the party, and subsequently went home.
words.ex_cn: 他离开了派对，随后回家了。
words.en: If something happens subsequently, it happens after something else.

words.ex: It rained all day, therefore the game was canceled.
words.ex_cn: 下了一整天的雨，因此比赛被取消了。
words.en: You use therefore to introduce a logical result or conclusion.

words.ex: He was late, so he left accordingly.
words.ex_cn: 他迟到了，于是相应地提前出发了。
words.en: In a way that is appropriate to the particular circumstances.

words.ex: He studied hard, as a result he passed the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习，结果通过了考试。
words.en: A phrase used to indicate that something is a consequence of a previous action or event.

words.ex: It rained all day, hence the game was canceled.
words.ex_cn: 下了一整天的雨，因此比赛被取消了。
words.en: You use hence to indicate that the statement you are about to make is a consequence of what you have just said.
